column1: # B888 (GitLab #204) character-creation era data. Read by include/client/login_world/char_create_data.h.
# Era filter (Will, 2026-09-23): a row whose era is not Classic, Kunark or Velious is HIDDEN -- never drawn,
# never offered, never sent; the in-era buttons are laid out without it. Columns per kind:
#   race  <xml button index> <wire race id> <label (XML <Text>)> <era> <eqstr description id>
#   class <xml button index> <wire class id> <label> <era> <eqstr description id>
#   deity <xml button index> <wire deity id> <label> <era> <eqstr description id>
#   city  <xml button index = CharCreate_Struct start_zone, the server's StartZoneIndex> <label> <era> <home zones>
#   cities  <race label|*> <class label|*> <deity label|*> <city labels, comma> <source>
# (CC0_Race0..14, CC0_Class0..15, CC1_Deity0..16, CC1_City0..14). Description ids: eqstr_us.txt, matched by text
# Wire ids: eqemu common/races.h, classes.h, deity.h. Agnostic is sent as 396 (Deity::Agnostic2) -- assumption
# awaiting the oracle pcap (140 is the other Agnostic id eqemu knows).
# Home zones: where the server puts that city's characters -- world/worlddb.cpp SetTitaniumDefaultStartZone() plus
# the neighbouring city zones a start_zones row may name (the table is not readable offline): assumption awaiting
# the oracle matrix (one measured landing: Human Ranger of Tunare, QEYNOS -> zone 3, qrg, at the Ranger guildmaster,
# review/UIGAP-ORACLE/204/14_after_create_entered_world_qeytoqrg.png). The create_character scenario accepts any of
# deities/cities rows: the official client greys what it does not offer for the chosen race/class(/deity). A row
# whose source names an oracle screenshot is MEASURED; "assumption" rows are fable's stand-in until the
# per-step oracle matrix lands (review/UIGAP-ORACLE/204/). Lookup: the most specific matching row wins
# (exact race+class+deity, then race+class, then race, then *). The server validates neither deity nor city for a
# Titanium client (CheckCharCreateInfoTitanium has no deity check; an unmatched start_zones row falls back to the
# city's default zone), so a wrong row here can mis-offer but cannot be refused.
